title: Backup Resilience
definition: The ability of a backup system to recover from errors, interruptions, and failures.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine your backup system as a bouncy ball. Sometimes, it gets stuck, but a quick nudge (like resetting a flag) helps it keep rolling. This keeps your data safe.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Backup resilience ensures the system can handle unexpected interruptions, such as Ctrl+C, power loss, or unmounting, by adding a trap to reset the backup flag, even in case of these interruptions.
difficulty_levels.expert: Backup resilience is not just about handling interruptions. It's about robustness in the face of various errors, including IO errors, permissions errors, and filesystem errors. It's about building a system that can learn from its mistakes and adapt to new challenges, even when they're not anticipated.

extra_fields.insight: The script's resilience can be improved by adding a trap to reset the backup flag, even in case of interruptions.
